test.title: Mechanical Properties of Solids - Test 3
test.description: Previous Year Questions as Chapter Test
test.syllabus: This test contains questions from all topics of this chapter included in the JEE Main syllabus. It includes a mix of questions from PYQs of JEE Main 2019 - 2025.

question.text: The length of a wire becomes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> when <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>120</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> tension are applied respectively. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math>, then the natural length of wire will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math>. Here the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is

The increase in pressure required to decrease the volume of a water sample by $0.2 \%$ is $\mathrm{P} \times 10^5 \mathrm{Nm}^{-2}$. Bulk modulus of water is $2.15 \times 10^9 \mathrm{Nm}^{-2}$. The value of P is $\ldots\ldots$
The elastic potential energy stored in a steel wire of length 20 m stretched through 2 cm is 80 J. The cross sectional area of the wire is _____ mm2. (Given, Y=2.0×1011 N m–2)

A body of mass m=10 kg is attached to one end of a wire of length 0.3 m. What is the maximum angular speed (in rad s-1) with which it can be rotated about its other end in a space station without breaking the wire?
[Breaking stress of wire σ=4.8×107 N m-2 and area of cross-section of the wire=10-2 cm2]

If average depth of an ocean is 4000 m and the bulk modulus of water is 2×109 N m-2, then fractional compression ΔVV of water at the bottom of ocean is α×10-2. The value of α is _______, (Given, g=10 m s-2, ρ=1000 kg m-3)

A steel wire of length 2 m and Young's modulus $2.0 \times 10^{11} \mathrm{Nm}^{-2}$ is stretched by a force. If Poisson ratio and transverse strain for the wire are 0.2 and $10^{-3}$ respectively, then the elastic potential energy density of the wire is _______ $\times 10^5$ (in SI units)

Two separate wires <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> are stretched by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> respectively, when they are subjected to a force of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo>.</mo></math> Assume that both the wires are made up of same material and the radius of wire <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn></math> times that of the radius of wire <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The length of the wires <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> are in the ratio of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>:</mo><mo> </mo><mi>b</mi><mo>.</mo></math> Then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></mfrac></math> can be expressed as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is _____.

The depth below the surface of sea to which a rubber ball be taken so as to decrease its volume by 0.02% is _____ m.

(Take density of sea water =103 kg m-3, Bulk modulus of rubber =9×108 N m-2, and g=10 m s-2)

A metal wire of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and cross-sectional area <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> has breaking stress <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>8</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. A block of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is attached at one end of the string and is rotating in a horizontal circle. The maximum linear velocity of block will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.

When a rubber ball is taken to a depth of _______ m in deep sea, its volume decreases by 0.5%
(The bulk modulus of rubber =9.8×108 N m-2 Density of sea water =103 kg m-3,g=9.8 m s-2)

A string of area of cross-section <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mm</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> and length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn></math> is connected with a rigid body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math>. The body is rotated in a vertical circular path of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The body acquires a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> at the bottom of the circular path. Strain produced in the string when the body is at the bottom of the circle is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></math>. (Use Young's modulus <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>11</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

A certain pressure '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math>' is applied to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math> litre of water and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math> litre of a liquid separately. Water gets compressed to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>01</mn><mo>%</mo></math> whereas the liquid gets compressed to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>03</mn><mo>%</mo></math>. The ratio of Bulk modulus of water to that of the liquid is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ______.

A wire of density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> is stretched between two clamps <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> apart. The resulting strain in the wire is  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>9</mn><mo> </mo><mo>×</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The lowest frequency of the transverse vibrations in the wire (Young's modulus of wire  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi><mo> </mo><mo>=</mo><mo> </mo><mn>9</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>10</mn></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi>Nm</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> ), (to the nearest integer),_______

Two metallic wires <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> have same volume and are made up of same material. If their area of cross sections are in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>:</mo><mo> </mo><mn>1</mn></math> and force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> is applied to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math>, an extension of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>∆</mo><mi>l</mi></math> is produced. The force which is required to produce same extension in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo> </mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mfrac></math> is ______.

Wires W1 and W2 are made of same material having the breaking stress of 1.25×109 N m-2. W1 and W2 have cross-sectional area of 8×10-7 m2 and 4×10-7 m2, respectively. Masses of 20 kg and 10 kg hang from them as shown in the figure. The maximum mass that can be placed in the pan without breaking the wires is _____kg (Use g=10 m s-2

The elongation of a wire on the surface of the earth is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The same wire of same dimensions is elongated by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> on another planet. The acceleration due to gravity on the planet will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. (Take acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

A steel rod has a radius of 20 mm and a length of 2.0 m. A force of 62.8 kN stretches it along its length. Young's modulus of steel is 2.0×1011N m-2. The longitudinal strain produced in the wire is _________×10-5.

The density and breaking stress of a wire are $6 \times 10^4 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$ and $1.2 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}^2$ respectively. The wire is suspended from a rigid support on a planet where acceleration due to gravity is $\frac{1}{3}^{\text {rd }}$ of the value on the surface of earth. The maximum length of the wire with breaking is _____ m (take, $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ ).

A wire of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>L</mi></math> and radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>r</mi></math> is clamped rigidly at one end. When the other end of the wire is pulled by a force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>F</mi></math>, its length increases by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. Another wire of the same material of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></math> and radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mi>r</mi></math> is pulled by a force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>F</mi></math> under same conditions. The increase in length of this wire is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>.

A uniform metallic wire is elongated by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>04</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> when subjected to a linear force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>F</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The elongation, if its length and diameter is doubled and subjected to the same force will be _________ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi><mo>.</mo></math>
